identityRule: Each record preserves one non-fileable Category B stage and records the absence of a participant Category A branch. Selector, output strategy, product outcome, and commercial treatment are separate fields and carry separate meanings.
commercialAuthority: These identities authorize no price, checkout, sponsorship, packet-credit use, provider dispatch, artifact attachment, delivery, repeat download, commercially eligible status, or COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN status.

routes.publicLabel: Records that clear automatically after a pardon

reuseDecision.basis: The exclusion is confirmed. The rcap-mn-guidance-implementation family contains route-specific guidance assets that can be extended without creating a filing branch.

identity.stageKind: After a qualifying pardon extraordinary is granted, expungement follows without a participant petition.

selector.scopeBoundary: The selector begins after the pardon extraordinary has been granted. It does not select or prepare the antecedent pardon application.

productOutcome.description: Explain the post-pardon duty, show the participant how to check the BCA and court records, and route a failed or disputed implementation to a human handoff.

commercialTreatment.reason: A participant files nothing on this stage, and the existing proof keeps the guidance family out of runtime and production.

participantABranch.reason: The post-pardon stage has no participant filing. The pardon application is a separate antecedent clemency route and is not created or crosswalked by this assignment.

routes.publicLabel: Where to go about a record from outside Nebraska

reuseDecision.basis: The exclusion is confirmed. The rcap-ne-guidance-implementation family contains route-specific routing assets that can be extended without creating a Nebraska filing branch.

identity.stageKind: Nebraska routes the participant to the sovereign that created the record because Nebraska cannot grant substantive relief for that record.

selector.governingCondition: The arrest, charge, or conviction was not created by a Nebraska court or Nebraska criminal-justice agency.
selector.coverageNote: The revalidation record also names foreign jurisdictions. The committed guidance selector has no foreign enum value, so this identity records the governing condition and does not invent a runtime value.

productOutcome.description: Identify the record's sovereign and custodian, separate any Nebraska records, and direct substantive relief to the originating court or repository.

commercialTreatment.reason: The route produces guidance and cannot sell a Nebraska filing that has no legal effect on the originating record.

participantABranch.reason: No Nebraska substantive-relief filing exists for the foreign record. The originating jurisdiction's remedy and any Nebraska repository data-correction process are separate routes and are not created or crosswalked here.

routes.publicLabel: Clearing a Virginia conviction vacated by a writ of actual innocence

reuseDecision.basis: The exclusion is confirmed. The rcap-va-guidance-implementation family contains route-specific explanation and verification assets that can be extended without creating a post-writ filing branch.

identity.stageKind: After a qualifying writ vacates the conviction and reaches the convicting circuit court, the court enters the expungement order and the clerk and record custodians transmit and implement it without a participant filing.

selector.scopeBoundary: The selector covers the downstream expungement stage. It does not select or prepare the antecedent writ litigation.

productOutcome.description: Explain the court's post-writ duty, help the participant confirm receipt and entry of the order, check the CCRE record, and route a stalled implementation back to counsel or the clerk.

commercialTreatment.reason: The participant files nothing after the writ, and the existing proof keeps the guidance family out of runtime and production.

participantABranch.reason: The post-writ stage has no participant filing. The writ petition is separate appellate post-conviction litigation and is not created or crosswalked by this assignment.
